analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the date and updates the GLM video description (lines 810-813 and 829) so that variable-frame-rate video is indexed by nominalFrameRate instead of being refused with a 400. It also adds prose on returned reasoning and strict tool validation (lines 876-880). No code, config or enforcement changes are visible in the supplied units, so no security control is changed by this PR itself.

The docs describe a behavior shift that the source must implement. A variable-frame-rate track is now accepted, and its frame timing is computed as i / nominalFrameRate. This could alter timestamps or frame sampling, but the bounds stay documented: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (`maximumDecodedBytes`), the 28,532 prepared-pixel visual-token cap, the VisionMemoryGate reservation, and deterministic 400s for processor refusals. The cap-enforcement code is not supplied, so I cannot verify that VFR inputs (e.g. a huge frame count with a low nominal rate) still stay inside those caps before decode. The next pass should check GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and GLM5NextVisionBudget in the code change, if there is one, for bounds on frame count and decode time under VFR.

The docs state that media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so there is no cross-tenant KV reuse via media. This is consistent with T-041 and is unchanged by this PR. The reasoning and strict-tool text (`returnedReasoning`, `ToolConstraintValidation.validate`) describes validation before exposure and adds no new trust boundary visible here.

I found no threat-model gaps or regressions in this docs-only change. Remaining uncertainty is limited to whether the paired code change enforces the decoded-frame cap under VFR input; that code is not in this batch.
